cells.tense: You are holding the line here, and the strain is being spent well.
cells.ask: Offer one piece of the work upward: show the one who could act what needs next, and then let the thing stay theirs to move — or not — without taking it back to prove it matters.
cells.core:
You're holding the line right now, and it's holding. Not because you're steel — because you know the difference between tension and support. What you carry sits in you without bending you, and the people near you can feel that. They lean on it more than they say.

The strain shows in the shape of your shoulders, not on your face, and you're nowhere near the edge. Tend it the way good things get tended. Say yes to one piece of this you actually want, out loud, and let the rest wait. Then what you carry keeps doing its quiet work, and the you inside it gets fed instead of spent.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying it in a way that holds.

cells.tense: You will keep holding past the point it is being carried, and the holding will become the whole task.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're already carrying and name its ending out loud: say what done looks like, and tell the person depending on it when you'll stop. Then stop there. If the work calls for a next step, they carry it.
cells.core:
You've set yourself to make it through, and you haven't decided what finishing looks like. Every loose end gets a little more grip than it needs. What steadiness looks like done well is simple: you carry a thing, and you can set it down when it's over. What you're doing is different. Bracing is doing the work of living, and the extra hours go into guarding a future you can't write in.

The bearing is fine. The way you're spending it isn't. There's a cleaner move than proving you'll last, and it isn't about surviving what comes. It's about ending it on purpose. Pick one load now and give it a finish.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding on ahead of the finish.

cells.tense: You learned somewhere back that asking was the price of carrying, and you haven't asked for anything since.
cells.ask: Set a stop time for one thing you said yes to today and hold that line instead of an extra hour. Finishing it early is allowed. Then tell one person it was heavy.
cells.core:
The effort goes into not needing anything from the room, and it's been going there a while. But the bank isn't empty — the asking stopped. When you're doing this well, you can stand under something heavy and still reach a hand out for help with it, and the help comes. That reach is gone now. The effort all goes one way, out, and nothing comes back to meet it. Nobody sees the bill, because it's paid quietly around the edges of what you do.

The way back is a body that rests, not a mind that decides to. Put weight down before you're finished, in small pieces someone could see. You'll find the room takes it better than you think, and resting now isn't knocking off early.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped asking to be held while you hold.

cells.tense: You are holding more for people than they know, and the holding is running without you in it.
cells.ask: Say to one person what you keep upright for them, plainly, so the standing becomes something you chose and said. That one saying is enough for today.
cells.core:
The dependent thing is already holding better because you decided it would. People have leaned on the arrangements without knowing the lean was yours, and you've called it the way it works. Not a lie, just a blind spot about who's been keeping it so. When nothing is missing, you know you're the one making the call, and you say so plainly.

You've earned the right to name it as yours. That's the repair: call the thing you're holding up something you chose, not something the room demanded. The ones you carry may have to move for it to stay theirs, but the choice stays yours either way.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding it up and nobody knows you chose to.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that they are already being seen by others; the record may only assert that being seen is the natural completion of what is given, not that a witness exists yet. A reader could object that their labor is genuinely unnoticed, or that they bent hardest for public credit and still got none. The asks survive that: each is one visible tending act, to say a true receipt, or to claim authorship of a holding, none requiring recognition to work. The sentence that serves me more than them is the line about the credit belonging to the person it belongs to; it names the whole status and does too much work, so I keep it out.
